answer.says: Ramesh, the cash in my pocket is not the cash of the household. The Directorate owes me, and I owe you, and the gap between us is not my fault, but it is my burden to bear. I cannot pay the full month's wage today. I will give you what I carry, and I will write to the Director tomorrow to expedite the arrears. You will come on Mondays and Thursdays, and I will ensure the cooking is maintained. Do not look at my purse with suspicion; look at the system. The system is broken, but we must keep the engine running.
answer.thought: The tension between my particular need for food and the universal duty of the state to its servants is acute. I hold the state as the actuality of the ethical idea, yet here the state is a paper labyrinth that starves its own caretaker. Ramesh's refusal to cook is not ingratitude; it is the rational response of a particular will to a failed universal promise. I must bridge this gap with my own substance, for the family, like the state, rests on the obedience of those who serve it.
